content.title: Weeknotes: The Other New Song — Week 31, 2026

content.html:
• Reader, this week I am looking at the world through new eyes.
  • Primed by some smaller conversations last weekend, a discussion about classifying cultures connected big dots in my head, and further reading/thinking/talking led me to an epiphany: I understood my identity for the first time:
    • You see, dear reader, being half, I am both of my nationalities, and yet paradoxically I am also neither. They form an interwoven tapestry where language for one describes the behaviours and thinking of the other, and vice versa. I was blind to this, and its effects.
    • When you look and sound like you’re from a place, people from the same place assume that’s all you are and expect a shared operating-system and language. And the differences grate, on both sides. You’re never truly an insider: It’s hard.
    • But the good news is that many people are in this same group: And throughout the week speaking to these others, my new in-group, about this has been genuinely freeing.
  • Anyway: Harry makes a damned good sandwich.
  • Starting to think everyone should have a monthly blood panel. Maybe Theranos were onto something.
  • Went to an all-day leadership training event this week which was useful and very fun. So fun, in fact, that I have been recommending its next batch to anyone who’ll listen.
  • After a networking event I kept on my name-tag. I joked it was in-case I got lost. And in some ways aren't we all? But I digress, this particular bit would’ve made more sense:
    1. To people who shared my encyclopaedic knowledge of sitcom tropes
    2. Had the name-tag contained a phone-number.
  • Anyway, then as CD approached me in the manner of a Rugby tackle, I positively legged it, before rendezvousing in an extremely smelly room for a succulent chinese meal: Kansai seems fun.
  • There is a lot of inner and outer work I am embarking on right now, and it is going to come at eyewatering cost which I am finally ready for.
  • Lollapalooza has been streaming this week and it’s excellent. Funny to see some Fujirock acts from last week appearing on this schedule. Surprise Charli during Lorde was my highlight.
  • Class is going very well, but I am disappointed in myself for not pushing myself to speak more broken Japanese more during the opportunities this week presented. Next week, eh.
  • Sunday lunch was good: Gorgonzola makes surprisingly good fondue sauce. I found myself seriously lost for words a few times but I also answered some big questions.
  • The wind sails over the water's surface.
